# New renderings and departures, iliad-050 (8.381–468)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ὣς ἔφατ’, οὐδ’ ἀπίθησε θεὰ λευκώλενος Ἥρη (8.381; the formula of 5.719, here with Athena speaking and Hera obeying: a departure from the published 5.719 wording, whose speaker is Hera, and from the "So he spoke" of the lines the packet lists, because the speaker here is a woman) | "So she spoke, and did not disobey, the goddess, white-armed Hera." | "So Athena spoke, and the goddess, white-armed Hera, did not disobey." | "So he spoke" (the speaker here is Athena, so ἔφατ’ is "she"); the speaker is named in `i`, as iliad-008 and iliad-034 name Hera |
| Ζεὺς δὲ πατὴρ Ἴδηθεν ἐπεὶ ἴδε χώσατ’ ἄρ’ αἰνῶς (8.397, whole line) | "And Zeus the father, from Ida, when he saw, was incensed dreadfully," | "When father Zeus saw them from Ida, he was dreadfully incensed," | "angry" (reserved for χόλος), "furious", "terribly angry"; χώομαι keeps "be incensed" and αἰνῶς "dreadfully" (1.555, 3.158) |
| χρυσόπτερον (Ἶριν, 8.398) | "gold-winged" | "gold-winged" | "golden-winged" (χρύσεος is "golden"), "with wings of gold"; χρυσο- "gold" as in χρυσάμπυξ, χρυσόθρονος |
| ἀγγελέουσαν · ἀγγελέουσα (8.398, 8.409) | "to tell the news" | "to bring news" | "to carry a message", "as a messenger" (ἀγγελίη is "news", "message" withdrawn); follows the table's ἀγγελίη rows ("tell news" in `l`, "bring news" in `i`) |
| ἀελλόπος (Ἶρις ἀελλόπος, 8.409; ἄελλα "storm" + πούς "foot", second part not quite certain) | "storm-footed" | "storm-footed" (+ note: second element not quite certain) | "wind-footed" (reserved for ποδήνεμος), "storm-swift", "storm-fleet", "with feet like a gale" |
| Ἶρι ταχεῖα (voc., 8.399) | "Iris swift" | "swift Iris" | "quick Iris"; ταχύς is "swift" as in the table's ταχέες πόδες, and the vocative gives the same English as ὠκέα Ἶρις "swift Iris" |
| βάσκ’ ἴθι (8.399) | "Go, set out" | "Be off with you" | "Go quickly", "Away with you"; follows the table's βάσκ’ ἴθι οὖλε ὄνειρε (2.8) |
| γυιώσω (γυιόω, 8.402, 8.416) | "I will lame" | "I will lame" | "I will cripple", "I will unnerve" (kept for ἀπογυιώσῃς, 6.264), "I will paralyse"; γυιόω is built on γυῖα "limbs" |
| ἕλκε’ ἀπαλθήσεσθον, ἅ κεν μάρπτῃσι κεραυνός (8.405, 8.419) | "will you two be healed of the wounds which the thunderbolt may seize" | "will you two be healed of the wounds that the thunderbolt may lay on you" | "cured", "recover from", "the bolt strikes"; μάρπτω is "seize" in `l`, and `i` takes the sense a wound needs |
| ἔωθεν ἐνικλᾶν (8.408, 8.422) | "she is accustomed to thwart" | "it is her habit to thwart me / him" | "obstruct", "oppose", "contradict", "break in on" (each decides the uncertain ἐνικλάω); ἔωθα "be accustomed" |
| ᾗ τελέει περ (8.415, sense not certain) | "as he will indeed fulfil it" | "and he will carry it out" (+ note: ᾗ uncertain) | "for he will surely do it", "truly he will fulfil it" (each decides between ᾗ and ἦ); τελέω keeps "fulfil" as in the table's Διὸς δ’ ἐτελείετο βουλή |
| πολυπτύχου Οὐλύμποιο (8.411; πολύς + πτυχ- "fold") | "many-folded Olympus" | "many-folded Olympus" | "many-ridged" (kept for πολυδειράς, 1.499), "of many folds", "of the deep valleys"; πτύχες "folds" of a mountain, as in the table's πτύχας ἠνεμοέσσας |
| πῇ μέματον; (8.413, μέμονα) | "Where are you two set on going?" | "Where are you two set on going?" | "Where are you heading?", "Where are you rushing to?"; μέμονα keeps "be eager, be set on" (compare the shipped "I am eager myself", 5.482) |
| ἐπαμυνέμεν (8.414) | "to come to the defence of" | "to come to the defence of" | "to come to the aid of" (first draft), "to help" (kept for ἀρήγω), "to ward off for" (ἀμύνω is "ward off"); follows the table's ἐπαμύνω (6.361) and ἐπάμυνον (5.685) "come to the defence of" |
| ἀδεές (κύον ἀδεές, 8.423; ἀδεής "without fear") | "fearless one" | "you fearless one" (+ note: vocative or adverb) | "shameless" (kept for ἀναιδής), "reckless", "bold", "fearlessly" (each decides between vocative and adverb) |
| κύον (vocative of a goddess, 8.423) | "dog" | "dog" | "bitch" (the Greek is the plain word κύων), "hound", "cur"; κύων "dog" as in the table |
| ἣ μὲν ἄρ’ ὣς εἰποῦσ’ ἀπέβη πόδας ὠκέα Ἶρις (8.425) | "She, indeed, then so having spoken went away, swift-in-feet Iris," | "So she spoke, and Iris, swift of foot, went away;" | "Iris of the swift feet"; follows the table's ἣ μὲν ἄρ’ ὣς εἰποῦσ’ ἀπέβη γλαυκῶπις Ἀθήνη (5.133, iliad-028) and πόδας ὠκέα Ἶρις |
| αὐτὰρ Ἀθηναίην Ἥρη πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπεν (8.426, whole-line speech introduction) | "but Athena Hera addressed with a word:" | "and Hera spoke to Athena:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο); follows the table's τὸν δ’ αὖτ’ ὀτρηρὴ ταμίη πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπεν (6.381) |
| οὐκέτ’ ἔγωγε νῶϊ ἐῶ (8.427–428) | "no longer I, for my part, the two of us allow" | "I no longer allow the two of us" | "let", "permit"; ἐάω keeps "allow" (1.276 "let it stand" is the idiom with an unstated object) |
| ὅς κε τύχῃ (8.430) | "whoever may chance" | "whichever it may chance to be" | "whoever is lucky", "whichever wins"; τυγχάνω with no object stated, said so in the note |
| τὰ ἃ φρονέων ἐνὶ θυμῷ (8.430, possessive ὅς) | "his own things thinking in his heart" | "thinking his own thoughts in his heart" | "keeping his own counsel", "minding his own business"; the possessive ὅς stays "his own" |
| ὣς ἄρα φωνήσασα πάλιν τρέπε μώνυχας ἵππους (8.432, whole line) | "So then, having spoken, back she turned the solid-hoofed horses;" | "So she spoke, and turned the solid-hoofed horses back;" | "wheeled", "turned about"; follows the table's ὣς ἄρα φωνήσας (6.116 shape, iliad-037) and μώνυχας ἵππους "solid-hoofed horses" |
| ἀμβροσίῃσι κάπῃσιν (8.434; κάπη "manger") | "the ambrosial mangers" | "the ambrosial mangers" | "stalls" (departure from the Odyssey's `i` "horse-stalls" at 4.40: a κάπη is a feeding-place, and the Odyssey's `l` already has "mangers"), "troughs" |
| ἅρματα δ’ ἔκλιναν πρὸς ἐνώπια παμφανόωντα (8.435) | "and the chariot they leaned against the shining inner wall;" | "and leaned the chariot against the gleaming inner wall;" | the Odyssey's wording (4.42) without "of the porch" in `i`: there the scene is a house with a porch (αἴθουσα), here the Greek names no porch |
| θεῶν θώκους (8.439) | "the council-seats of the gods" | "the gods’ seats of council" | "thrones", "assembly"; follows the table's θῶκος "council-seat" / "the seat of council" (Odyssey 15.468) |
| ἐΰτροχον ἅρμα (8.438) | "well-rolling chariot" | "well-rolling chariot" | "well-wheeled" (kept for ἐύκυκλος), "smooth-running"; follows the table's ἄμαξα ἐύτροχος "well-rolling" |
| κλυτὸς ἐννοσίγαιος (8.440) | "the famous earth-shaker" | "the famous earth-shaker" | follows the table unchanged |
| βωμοῖσι (ἂμ βωμοῖσι, 8.441) | "upon the pedestals" | "on its pedestals" | "stands" (first draft), "altars" (no sacrifice is in view; the note says the word is usually "altar"); follows the table's βωμός (7.100) "pedestal" where no sacrifice is in view |
| κατὰ λῖτα πετάσσας (8.441) | "spreading a linen cloth over it" | "spreading a linen cloth over it" | follows the table's λῖτα "linen cloth" (Odyssey 10.353) |
| τίφθ’ οὕτω τετίησθον (8.447) | "Why so are you two grieved" | "Why are you two so grieved" | "troubled", "downcast", "sad" in `l`; τετιημένος ἦτορ is "grieved in the heart" in the table, and the dual keeps "grieved" |
| οὐ μέν θην κάμετον (8.448) | "Surely you have not grown weary, I suppose" | "Surely you two have not grown tired of" | "I think you cannot have", "you cannot possibly"; θήν "surely, I suppose" |
| κότον αἰνὸν ἔθεσθε (8.449) | "a fearsome resentment you have set up" | "you have taken up a fearsome resentment" | "terrible hatred", "bitter grudge" (κότος is "resentment", χόλος "anger"); αἰνός "fearsome" as in the table's τρόμος αἰνός |
| ἄαπτοι (χεῖρες ἄαπτοι, 8.450; sense and origin uncertain) | "invincible" | "invincible" (+ note: sense uncertain) | "untouchable", "unapproachable", "irresistible" (each decides the uncertain sense) |
| μέρμερα ἔργα (8.453; sense uncertain) | "baneful deeds" | "baneful deeds" (+ note: origin uncertain) | "grievous" (reserved for ἀλεγεινός), "cruel", "grim", "dreadful" (reserved for δεινός) |
